title: Psychological safety in neonatal teams in Germany: a nationwide cross-sectional survey
summary:
Background: In wards that care for unwell newborns and premature babies, doctors and nursing staff work closely together. The work is demanding and emotionally taxing. For a team to work well together, everyone must feel confident enough to ask questions, raise issues and admit mistakes without fear of negative consequences. This feeling is known as psychological safety. It is considered vital for teamwork, the safety of the children and the well-being of staff. To date, little is known about this in Germany with regard to wards caring for sick newborns.
Research question: We wish to find out how doctors and nursing staff in Germany experience psychological safety within their teams. We are also interested in whether there are differences between professional groups, age groups and levels of professional experience.
Methodology: We are conducting a Germany-wide survey. Medical and nursing staff from wards caring for sick newborns and preterm babies are eligible to take part, regardless of their professional experience. Participants will complete a one-off online questionnaire based on two previously validated questionnaires on this topic. It takes approximately 5 minutes to complete. Participation is voluntary and anonymous; it is not possible to identify individual participants. The results will be analysed in summary form and published in a scientific journal.

interventions.name: Questionnaire survey amongst neonatal teams (medical and nursing) throughout Germany

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical and nursing staff working in a neonatal unit in Germany
Exclusion criteria:
Staff who do not work in the neonatal unit or who are not doctors or nurses
